Developer reference

Find a capability, contract, or method

This page is for developers integrating a capability; people who use applications find the install steps on the Adopt page.

OpenAbstractions gives applications stable capability APIs above operating systems, local engines, and remote services. This page defines the shared vocabulary, shows the service lifecycle, and indexes the current APIs.

The latest runtime release notes identify the available packages and their verification. The retained 0.3.0 evidence describes that release. Capability SDKs have independent versions. Match package availability and installation evidence to the API you adopt.

Shared vocabulary

Terms used across capabilities

Words you'll meet first

Runtime
The OA background service installed on the machine. Every application talks to this one program.
Client library (facade)
The OA library an application adds to find the runtime and get a typed client for each capability.
Provider
The program that does the work behind a capability, such as curl for a download or Ollama for a model call.
Capability
One kind of work OA offers through one API, such as downloads, jobs, model calls or questions to the person.
Operator
The person who runs the machine, acting at the command line or in the Panel.
Permission
What an application may do on this machine, which the person allows or blocks per program.
Question
A request for a person's decision. Applications present their ordinary choices; OA presents its permission requests. The service retains pending and answer state.
Job
Work the runtime accepted and keeps running after the application closes, with progress and a result to read later.
Host (asks.application-host)
The receiving application-question service that admits questions through a configured book, binds callers and checks its configured operator and responder authorization.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Host owns the receiving application-question listener, bound caller and configured Book/authorization callbacks. It is a service host, distinct from a model-server host or a UI window (application/host.go; asks.thrift). No external interface-equivalence or historical naming decision is asserted. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): Case.Host is a boolean in the script-host classification fixture; Host remains the application-question receiving service object. Exact neighbouring declarations: Case.Host.

Question book (asks.book)
The asks service keeps admitted questions and their recorded answers in a durable Book, using explicitly separate storage profiles for current application questions and deprecated native questions.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: Book is the service-owned durable question/answer storage shared by separately loaded current application and deprecated native formats (book.go; application_book.go; ASK-A3/P1/P3). Application replay and authority rules belong to that profile, not every legacy Book. NativePermission1472 retains AskTypedPermissionOccurrenceAuthorizedFrom for trusted finite-service occurrence replay/coalescing and AnswerTypedPermissionAsResponderAuthorized for an actual attributed answer under trusted host eligibility; typed_permission.go185/326 and ASK-A11/R3/R4. These are Book operations, not independent storage concepts.

Ask (asks.question-ask)
A request to admit or replay a service-owned catalogue question by key and slots, with optional legacy peer context that supplies no authority.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Ask carries a catalogue key and slots for admitting/replaying a service-owned question; optional legacy peer observation supplies context and grants no authority. This bounded request differs from arbitrary prompt text (wire.go; CONTRACT.md ASK-A2/A3/A5). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): The legacy Request.Ask holds the native Ask, while the generated Request.Ask holds the schema Question. Both are request payload slots, with admission and actor binding still owned by the service. Exact neighbouring declarations: Request.Ask.

Record (asks.question-history-record)
A retained question with its catalogue text and options, admission and answer times, selected answer and recorded actor provenance; the answer itself grants no resource permission.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Record retains catalogue wording/options, admission and answer times and observed actor provenance. It records question history; an answer is not resource authorization (wire.go; asks.thrift). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): The choice fields carry ChoiceRecord, notification fields carry NotificationRecord, and operator/responder metadata fields carry RecordMetadata. Those typed histories retain their own schemas; the native Record retains the application question and its admitted/answered provenance. Exact neighbouring declarations: ChoiceAttribution.Record, ChoiceCandidate.Record, ChoiceDecision.Record, ChoicePage.Records, ChoiceRead.Record, NotificationDecision.Record, NotificationPage.Records, NotificationRead.Record, OperatorDecision.Record, OperatorPage.Records, OperatorQuestion.Record, OperatorRetirement.Record, ResponderDecision.Record, ResponseMetadata.Records.

QuestionOperator (asks.question-operator)
The authorized service interface for listing retained application questions, recording catalogue answers and retiring questions while preserving admission history.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): QuestionOperator is the authorized catalogue-question control service for listing, conditional answering and retirement; its generated interface and retained history belong to asks.thrift. The service is distinct from a human operator and the client wrapper.

Question operator client (asks.question-operator-client)
The question operator client calls a selected asks service to list retained questions, record a catalogue answer or retire a question, with permission checked by the receiving service.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: Apache Thrift Go tutorial uses a generated client over a selected transport (https://thrift.apache.org/tutorial/go.html). OA client.Operator wraps QuestionOperator with context, bounds and response validation; D29 supplies its human-tool naming role, while ASK-O1 owns authorization. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): AnswererRule.Operators contains eligible operator program strings; Host.operator is an AuthorizeOperator callback. Neither is the context-aware Operator client handle. Exact neighbouring declarations: AnswererRule.Operators, Host.operator.

Change (cas.change)
Edit one file while holding its shared compare-and-set lock across reading the current bytes, applying the callback and replacing the value.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Change holds one file lock across read, callback edit and replacement; Write instead compares an explicit earlier base. Ordinary file writes do not define this transaction (cas.go; README.md Words; https://pkg.go.dev/os#WriteFile).

Read (cas.read-file)
Read the current bytes of one file for compare-and-set work, returning no value when the file is absent and preserving other filesystem errors.

Source: Go os.ReadFile whole-file read, https://pkg.go.dev/os#ReadFile. OA Read preserves its content operation and explicitly maps an absent file to no value for compare-and-set; other filesystem errors remain errors (cas.go).

Write (cas.write-file)
Replace a file only when its current presence and bytes match the supplied base, with comparison and replacement protected by the shared file lock.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Write compares current presence/bytes with the supplied base under the shared file lock before staged replacement. Go os.WriteFile creates/truncates a file without this base precondition; the OA name denotes conditional replacement (cas.go; CONTRACT.md CAS-L1/L2; https://pkg.go.dev/os#WriteFile).

Config (config.machine-settings)
Resolved machine, user, environment and default settings for job stores and service locations, with the source of each key retained as provenance.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Config combines optional machine/user/environment/default job-store and logging settings, with per-key origin provenance. It is this selected configuration document, distinct from the service client or an application permission policy (config.go). No external precedence standard is claimed.

Observer (config.observer-client)
A reusable client of the latest-configuration observation service, using a cursor and explicit run overrides to request bounded waits for settings changes.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Observer is a reusable authenticated client for latest configuration snapshots, caller run overrides and a bounded cursor wait. It is not a retained event stream or the settings object itself (client/observer.go; config.thrift).

Credential applier service (credentials.applier-service)
The credential applier service checks a designated enforcer’s subject, consumer, target and permission for one credential use, and returns request headers only when Apply succeeds.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation (2026-10-24): Applier is the receiver-owned Check/Apply boundary under credentials/applier@1 (credentials.thrift; CRED-A1-A5). It applies a saved credential inside an authorized service after scope and rights checks; construction conveys neither a grant nor raw-reader authority. No OAuth service equivalence or historical rejection is claimed.

Backend (credentials.backend)
One configured platform secret store with opaque-key put, get and delete operations, store identity and size limits, preserving confirmed absence separately from an unreachable store.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Backend adapts platform secret stores to opaque-key Put/Get/Delete plus identity and size bounds, preserving unavailable versus confirmed absence. Windows CredWrite creates/updates a user credential and Secret Service manages items/locking; neither defines this OA error/interface contract (backend.go; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincred/nf-wincred-credwritew; https://specifications.freedesktop.org/secret-service/latest/).

Scope (credentials.credential-scope)
The target host names and applying service-contract names on which a credential may be used; the credential service checks both before applying the secret.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Scope is the exact target-host and applying-consumer-contract allowlist attached to a credential. It constrains where a designated enforcer may apply that secret; it is distinct from placement or a reusable authorization grant (credentials.thrift Scope; CONTRACT.md CRED-A2). Scope retains the published record codec language across holder@1/holder@2 and applier@1/applier@2; Holder owns semantic use validation.

Limits (credentials.holder-limits)
The credential provider's reported count, secret-size, retention and audit bounds, configured secure store and supported credential kinds. A refused listing carries zero bounds and no store name.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): credentials.thrift Limits is the provider-declared listing metadata described by CONTRACT.md and returned in MetadataPage. It reports bounds and store capabilities; it grants no credential access. This current-source description establishes no historical rejection or industry novelty.

Applications (facade.applications-client)
The context-aware client handle that resolves the local application-presence service and calls its generated wire client through the shared authenticated transport.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Applications is the context-aware client handle that resolves the local applications@2 directory and delegates to the generated wire client through FrameClient. Its transport/lifetime wrapper is distinct from the generated Applications service interface (client/applications.go). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): The appmodel query/call Application strings identify a registered application and listing fields carry ListedApplication/ApplicationListing values. Runtime Host.applications and Options.Applications hold ApplicationsService. The native Applications client is the caller handle, with no authority supplied by those directory fields. Exact neighbouring declarations: ApplicationListing.Applications, ApplicationsQuery.Application, CallRecord.Application, CommandListing.Application, CommandsQuery.Application, Envelope.Applications, GatewayCall.Application, Host.applications, ListedApplication.Application, Options.Applications. ActivateRequest.Application and ChangeRequest.Application are selected registered application names in the new applications@3 requests; the scoped native Applications interface operates those requests, while client.Applications remains the legacy context-aware handle. AgentEnrollment.Application, AgentEnrollmentRequest.Application, AgentUpdateMember.Application and AgentUpdateImage.Application identify the existing registered directory entry; Applications remains the service interface and its scoped native caller representation operating those records. OriginClaim.Application is only unverified remote-origin display/receipt-namespace metadata; it is not this Applications service or native enrollment proof. SetupRequest.Application is the requesting app's display name a pending setup request hands the presenter for its question; it identifies no entry and is not this Applications service. Registration.Applications holds observed ApplicationReading values; RegistrationSpec.Applications holds submitted ApplicationFacet values. Applications names the service operating application-facet methods. ApplicationOpenVerbs.Application identifies a listing group. ConnectExpectation.Application identifies the single app selected for the Panel’s Connect expectation. Applications names the native service interface and the scoped caller handle. KeptApplicationClassTarget.Application identifies the target application in one exact Rights selection. StartRecord.Application names the app whose native process cohort the shared stop record holds. Applications is the directory interface and its caller handle.

Applications (facade.applications-rpc)
The generated application-presence service interface for registration, announcement, observation and activation; directory metadata grants no invocation authority.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Applications is the generated applications@2 service for registration, presence, observation and activation. Its directory metadata confers no invocation authority; the client handle remains a separate wrapper (facade.thrift; go-core generated API). D-Bus activation is comparative prior art, not this API: https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#message-bus-starting-services. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): ApplicationPage.Applications contains ApplicationEntry values, while ApplicationPresence.Application and ApplicationStart.Application identify the named application. Applications remains the service interface operating those records. Exact neighbouring declarations: ApplicationPage.Applications, ApplicationPresence.Application, ApplicationStart.Application.

Caller observation service (facade.caller-observation-service)
The caller observation service reports native identity evidence established for the calling connection, including the proof and transport ceiling for each attribute, for diagnostics.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: Credentials describes retrieved peer facts in D-Bus GetConnectionCredentials; Caller is OA-specific connection-scoped diagnostic echo with per-attribute proof and ceiling, with no rights decision (facade.thrift Caller; RESOLUTION.md caller section). Primary comparison: https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#bus-messages-get-connection-credentials.

Activation (facade.declaration-activation)
A provider declaration's activation mode: supervised on-demand launch, attachment to an existing provider or connection to a configured remote runtime.

Source: D-Bus Specification, Message Bus Starting Services (Activation), https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#message-bus-starting-services: activation starts an application for a named service. OA adapts that established term to its declaration modes on_demand, attach and remote; the latter two and OA supervision/trust rules are explicit OA composition (facade.thrift Activation). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): ApplicationDescriptor.Activation is an ApplicationActivationRecipe containing the declared recipe; Activation is the enum selecting the declaration activation mode. Exact neighbouring declarations: ApplicationDescriptor.Activation.

Description (facade.endpoint-description)
An endpoint's description of its own program, version and services; a refused response clears the identity and service fields.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Description is an endpoint@1 response naming that endpoint program/version and advertised service readiness. Refusals clear the identity/services; description is neither caller proof nor capability-call success (facade.thrift Description; CONTRACT.md FAC-B1..B3).

ServiceState (facade.endpoint-service-state)
A service-state report identifies one contract hosted by an endpoint, its readiness and reason, the provider's stated guarantees and display capabilities. These fields grant no authority.

Source: The gRPC Health Checking Protocol associates a service name with its reported serving status. OA's ServiceState similarly reports one hosted contract's readiness; its reason, stated guarantees and display capabilities are specified by facade.thrift and CONTRACT.md FAC-B1/B2 and confer no authority. This comparison establishes no equivalence of those additional fields. https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md ; https://github.com/grpc/grpc-proto/blob/master/grpc/health/v1/health.proto

Machine (facade.machine-client)
The application's typed facade client for selecting a configured runtime and resolving capability bindings through it.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Machine is the typed application facade client that selects registered runtime evidence and resolves capability bindings. The name denotes access through the selected runtime, not ownership of a physical machine or a configuration origin (client/client.go). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): MachinePage.Machines contains MachineRecord directory entries; Machine remains the selected-runtime client facade, not one of those directory records. Exact neighbouring declarations: MachinePage.Machines.

Subject (facade.probe-subject)
A probe subject displays the probe process's current account and executable path.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: probe.Subject displays Self's diagnostic account and executable (probe/probe.go); its fields supply no receiving-peer authority. The researched XACML 3.0 section 1.1.1 Subject instead names the policy actor whose access is evaluated, a role this display does not perform. https://docs.oasis-open.org/xacml/3.0/xacml-3.0-core-spec-os-en.html Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): CallRecord.Subject is appmodel diagnostic subject text; probe.Subject is a diagnostic account/program pair. Neither representation proves the receiving actor for an authorization decision. Exact neighbouring declarations: CallRecord.Subject. Header.Subject and SendRequest.Subject in Messages are untrusted message headlines; probe.Subject instead displays the diagnostic account/program pair. PrepareRequest.Subject is also an untrusted new-message headline, not probe.Subject or an authenticated policy actor (messages.thrift; native Messages disposition P-J15, 942ae8aec). Publisher.Subject is observed publisher distinguished-name display. probe.Subject displays the process account and executable.

RemoteTrust (facade.registry-remote-trust)
Configuration selecting a remote runtime's certificate name, trusted roots and local client certificate and key files, with an optional remote credential designation.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): RemoteTrust holds configured certificate server name, root/client PEM paths and an optional credential designation for one remote runtime. RFC8446 supplies TLS1.3 certificate authentication; these registry configuration fields and OA caller mapping are separate composition (facade.thrift; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html). No secret key bytes travel in the declaration.

Provider registry service (facade.registry-service)
An authorized local operator lists, declares, withdraws and observes provider declarations and their readings, with each operation requiring provider.manage permission for the bound operator.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: ListNames lists current D-Bus bus names; Registry is the OA operator-owned declaration/readings lifecycle with provider.manage and conditional revisions, including programs and remote hosts (facade.thrift Registry). Primary comparison: https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#bus-messages-list-names.

Service resolver (facade.resolver-service)
An application asks the receiving runtime to select an authorized ready provider matching an exact service contract, required guarantees and placement, then authenticates and calls the returned candidate separately.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: GetNameOwner resolves a D-Bus name to its owning connection; Resolver selects an OA candidate by authority, exact contract, readiness, guarantees and placement (facade.thrift Resolver; RESOLUTION.md). Primary comparison: https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#bus-messages-get-name-owner.

Binding (facade.service-binding)
A facade service binding supplies the call transport and read-only provider reference selected for one exact capability contract.

Source: Microsoft RPC Binding Handles (2020-08-19) supplies the logical client/server connection meaning. OA client.Binding associates the resolved call transport and read-only provider reference with an exact capability contract (client/resolved.go; CONTRACT.md FAC-B4); its transport and representation follow OA's contract. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/rpc/binding-handles Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): InventoryClient.binding is its JobsClient handle. Binding remains the resolved capability transport/reference tie; the field stores the inventory caller used to reach the job capability. Exact neighbouring declarations: InventoryClient.binding.

ServiceReference (facade.service-reference)
One candidate capability binding with its provider, exact contract, guarantees, placement, transport and opaque endpoint; calling it still requires authentication and authorization.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): ServiceReference names one resolver candidate by provider, exact capability/contract, guarantees, placement and opaque transport/endpoint. The record is selection metadata and carries no caller authority or proof that a provider call succeeded (facade.thrift; RESOLUTION.md).

FrameClient (identity.frame-client)
The caller-side framed request client, configured with an endpoint, waiting and payload bounds, optional server trust and connection-session selection. It adapts the caller's context for each operation.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): listen/framed.go FrameClient implements bounded caller-side exchanges; listen/FRAMING.md owns framing, context and session behavior. This records the current implementation, not a standard-defined type or historical naming rejection.

Sessions (identity.frame-sessions)
Reuse one connection and its captured binding for sequential bounded framed exchanges, rechecking the peer and the request's proof requirement before each dispatch.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Sessions reuses one authenticated connection/binding for sequential bounded framed requests, rechecking each exchange and preserving the single-exchange path. This is OA framing lifetime, not generic multiplexing or a new proof level (listen/session.go; listen/FRAMING.md Sessions). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): FrameClient.Sessions is the boolean selecting reusable authenticated sessions; Sessions is the receiving session policy/handler composition implementing that lifetime. Exact neighbouring declarations: FrameClient.Sessions.

Listener program evidence requirement (identity.listener-program-need)
The listener's Program evidence requirement asks for kernel evidence of the incoming caller account and process plus a bound executable path.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: A process identifier from GetNamedPipeClientProcessId is one OS observation; Program is the OA listener minimum combining kernel account/process and bound path evidence before delivery (listen/listen.go Program and Receive; identity CONTRACT). Primary comparison: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-getnamedpipeclientprocessid. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): ServerExpectation.Program and Subject.Program are executable/program-name strings; Program is the listener proof minimum requiring a bound program identity, not the path string alone. Exact neighbouring declarations: ServerExpectation.Program, Subject.Program.

Binding (identity.peer-binding)
An identity binding retains a captured native peer and platform evidence for rechecking that capture.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: identity.Binding retains native peer evidence for rechecking a capture; RetainProcess can retain an independent process pin on supported platforms (bind.go; CONTRACT.md receiving-identity lifetime). The researched RFC 5056 section 2 channel binding compares authenticated protocol layers at both endpoints to detect MITM; that cross-layer comparison does not describe this native evidence lifetime. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5056.html#section-2 Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): Limits.Binding is the transport binding-name string in attainable-proof information; Binding is retained native evidence used for capture rechecks. Exact neighbouring declarations: Limits.Binding.

Ceiling (identity.proof-ceiling)
The strongest native identity evidence the running platform can establish for each attribute, with reasons for its limits, independently of any captured connection.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Ceiling reports the strongest native evidence each attribute can reach on the running platform, with reasons. It is independent of a captured peer and distinct from a listener requirement or that connection's proof (identity.go; CONTRACT.md ID-L1).

Identity proof limits (identity.proof-limits)
For a selected transport on the running platform, proof limits describe the strongest available evidence for each native identity attribute and explain binding support and stronger transports.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: Credentials reports observed client fields in sd_bus_get_name_creds; Limits reports the best attainable proof before any connection and its transport-dependent reasons, used to refuse impossible policies at startup (CONTRACT ID-L1/L2/L5/L6; peer.go Limits). Primary comparison: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/sd_bus_get_name_creds.html. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): FramedCall.limit is a uint32 payload bound for one framed exchange; Limits is the structured attainable-identity-proof report. Exact neighbouring declarations: FramedCall.limit.

Server (identity.remote-server)
A TLS 1.3 frame server with explicit certificate trust, live exact-key peer admission and bounded concurrent request handlers.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): Server composes TLS1.3 authenticated peers with live exact-key admission and bounded OA frame handlers. RFC8446 defines TLS authentication, not OA handler limits, pin policy or request semantics (remote/server.go; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html). Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): FrameClient.Server is a ServerExpectation used to authenticate the selected endpoint; remote.Server is the bounded TLS receiving owner. Exact neighbouring declarations: FrameClient.Server.

SealedResourceEvidence (identity.sealed-resource-evidence)
The opaque owner of captured bundle-resource bytes authenticated by every supported main-program slice's trusted signature. It returns copied bytes, compares the exact signed code of an actual received XPC request, and releases its retained evidence through synchronized Close.

Source: Accepted source-specific composition (research/vocabulary/DECISION.md sections 1-2 and 9 C1): the Go owner of captured plain-resource bytes authenticated through each supported app-main-code slice's platform-trusted signature and resource seal, retaining exact signed-code requirements for an actual received XPC request. Source: CONTRACT ID-M5; sealed_resource.go:18-30,146-191; sealed_resource_native_darwin.c:9-15,36-86. The state field retains the private serialized data/native owner; Bytes returns a copy and Close releases that state. Apple Security's SecCodeValidateFileResource and SecCodeCheckValidity supply the underlying resource/signature meanings; this row records the precise OA composition rather than an Apple type name.

VerifySealedResource (identity.sealed-resource-verification)
The operation that verifies bounded captured resource bytes beneath the provided local app bundle and actual main program. It returns opaque evidence for trusted signatures on every supported slice, plus Code and Proof for the natively selected slice; unsupported platforms return ErrUnimplemented.

Source: Accepted source-specific composition (research/vocabulary/DECISION.md sections 1-2 and 9 C1): the ID-M5 verification operation over borrowed bundle/program fileid.Handle values, a policy-owned Resources/ relative name and positive byte bound. Source: sealed_resource.go:33-42,57-132; sealed_resource_darwin.go:42-132; CONTRACT ID-M5. It captures through fileid.Beneath, validates the actual main program and every supported slice on fresh Security objects, and returns SealedResourceEvidence plus the native selected Code/Proof. VerifyFile retains its separate file-display contract; this operation supplies captured-resource and exact-request comparison evidence. Unsupported builds return ErrUnimplemented (sealed_resource_other.go:13-15).

BindStartedProcess (identity.started-process-binding)
The Go native operation that captures a caller-owned unreaped child as an existing Binding. On Darwin it retains the original task and kernel audit occurrence, reports actual process generation and audit session, and refuses uncertain evidence; unsupported platforms return ErrUnimplemented.

Source: Accepted source-specific composition (research/vocabulary/DECISION.md sections 1-2 and 9 C1; CONTRACT ID-M5): started_process.go BindStartedProcess returns the existing Binding for a caller-owned unreaped os.Process. started_process_native_darwin.c oa_started_process_create checks the live direct child, retains a task-name right and captures its kernel audit token; fresh token-selected code checks end authority on exec or exit. User, Process and Path retain their distinct observed principal, occurrence and image roles. The caller serializes capture against Wait/Release; FindProcess alone establishes no ownership. Unsupported builds return ErrUnimplemented. This operation supplies process evidence and conveys no application rights or initializer containment.

Provider (inference.chat-provider)
The serving object that checks a bound caller, selects a model host, starts model work and retains updates for that caller to observe or cancel.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: gRPC Introduction distinguishes a server implementation of a service interface from the client stub that calls it (https://grpc.io/docs/what-is-grpc/introduction/, Overview). OA Provider names the serving runtime object that applies bound-subject admission/credential checks and retains chat operations (provider.go; INF-A1/A2/Q1/Q2). Model host names the selected execution target; client.Chat names the caller wrapper. Provider preserves those roles without claiming gRPC wire compatibility, standard-defined Provider terminology or historical rejection. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): SelectionCandidateV2.Provider is the selected provider name string; Provider is the serving runtime object that enforces admission and retains operations. Exact neighbouring declarations: SelectionCandidateV2.Provider.

Chat (inference.chat-service)
The chat@1 service interface for admitting model work and observing or cancelling the resulting operation for the receiving runtime's bound caller. Operations are visible to the account and program that started them.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): inference.thrift Chat is the generated abstraction.inference/chat@1 service interface. Its receiving runtime binds the caller and owns admission and operation visibility. client.Chat is the context-aware caller wrapper; gateway.Chat is a subject-aware provider dependency. ChatV3Session.Chat is a chat@3 client session's ChatV3Observation handle for observing and cancelling its request. This records current OA source, not historical rejection or industry novelty.

Admission (inference.operation-admission)
The result of asking to start one model operation: acceptance supplies its identifier, selected host and model, and observation bounds; refusal supplies a reason and no operation.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: Google AIP-151 returns a longrunning.Operation token for progress/result and distinguishes errors preventing start from execution errors (https://google.aip.dev/151, Guidance and Errors). OA Admission names the separate Start decision with accepted operation/host/model and retention/idle bounds, or a refusal with empty identity and zero bounds (INF-A2; inference.thrift Admission). Operation would blur that decision with the later retained work; StartOutcome names only its category. No Google operation wire/API compatibility or historical rejection is claimed. Current neighbour review (2026-10-25): Host.admission is a sync.RWMutex protecting admission work; Admission is the Start decision record, not the synchronization primitive. Neighbour review (2026-11-05): ChatV3Session.Admission retains the chat@3 ChatAdmission returned by Open's single Start. Exact neighbouring declarations: Host.admission, ChatV3Session.Admission.

Delta (inference.operation-delta)
One numbered update in a model operation, carrying a piece of output, usage, progress or its terminal reply; callers read retained updates in sequence.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: WHATWG Server-sent events carries event data and an id string, with Last-Event-ID on reconnection (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html, sections9.2.4-9.2.6). OA Delta names one typed numbered update read through bounded Observe pages, with explicit retained-window gaps and a terminal profile reply (INF-Q2; inference.thrift Delta/DeltaPage). Event alone would omit these operation-specific payload/retention rules. This comparison establishes no SSE encoding or delivery equivalence and no historical rejection.

DeltaPage (inference.operation-delta-page)
A bounded observation result containing retained operation updates, the next sequence and an end flag, with explicit retention-gap and refusal outcomes.

OA adaptation: Current OA composition (2026-10-24): DeltaPage is the bounded retained-update Observe result with next sequence, end and gap/refusal outcomes. It pages OA operation history; it is distinct from an individual Delta or an unbounded push stream (inference.thrift DeltaPage; CONTRACT.md INF-Q2).

Binding (job.acceptance-binding)
A job acceptance binding carries the receiver-established caller scope and any authenticated subject and provenance evidence used to admit durable work.

OA adaptation: Receipt is recoverable admission evidence. Binding packages receiver-produced scope with optional authenticated subject and provenance evidence for admission (acceptanceprovider/subject.go; JOB-A1).

Receipt (job.acceptance-receipt)
A job acceptance receipt binds a request identity to its stable logical owner, operation, accepted guarantees and minimum history retention. Its identifiers grant no authority, and replay does not renew retention.

Source: HTTP Semantics RFC 9110 section 15.3.3 describes acceptance with a status-monitor reference; Google AIP-151 returns an operation reference for later progress and results. These are acceptance/status-reference comparisons. OA's recoverable request/owner binding, guarantees and retention are specified by acceptance.thrift and CONTRACT.md JOB-A2/A3/A5; the compared protocols do not promise those OA fields. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.3.3 ; https://google.aip.dev/151

Job FileStore (job.file-store)
The job FileStore keeps one durable job record per file under a local root and changes each record through compare-and-swap.

OA adaptation: Current OA implementation adaptation documented 2026-10-24: the job Store file binding keeps one JSON record per job under a normative local root and applies edits with cas.Change (store.go:17-22,80-95). CONTRACT.md section "The deprecated job store and managed ownership" retains the runtime execution-store role and deprecates direct application use; the CAS package FileStore is a distinct direct adapter.

A job intent records a requested run, pause or cancel state, with the requester and time, independently of the execution lease.

OA adaptation: Current OA adaptation accepted 2026-10-24: Kubernetes spec/status separates desired from observed state (https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/). OA Intent applies that distinction to an immutable-spec job: run/pause/cancel is a separate requester-and-time field writable without the execution lease; JOB-I1/I3/I7/I8/I9 and job.thrift Intent govern it. GeneratedRecords1722 neighbour: InputRecord.Intent is the private legacy/proposal input member carrying this existing native meaning through the canonical job.thrift nested codec (or State string) and typed record.go adapter; it grants no additional authority.

A job lease is exclusive, time-bounded ownership of one job record; renewal keeps it alive, and writes present its acquisition epoch.

A yield request moves expiry earlier (JOB-R3). DECISION D89 keeps the qualified job sense. https://github.com/openabstractions/abstraction-job/blob/main/CONTRACT.md GeneratedRecords1722 neighbour: InputRecord.Lease is the private legacy/proposal input member carrying this existing native meaning through the canonical job.thrift nested codec (or State string) and typed record.go adapter; it grants no additional authority.

Card
A graphics card's memory; card:0 names the first one.
Adopter
An application that uses OA, such as OpenCode or ComfyUI with their OA integrations.
CAS (compare-and-set)
OA's small-file update that writes only when the file still holds the value the writer last read. Content-addressed storage is the storage module's job.

All terms

Abstraction
A stable concept and API whose meaning holds across operating systems, libraries, engines, and service providers. Each abstraction can be adopted independently.
Capability
The work an application asks OA to supply, such as reading content, submitting durable work, routing a model, or asking a user a question. One or more modules implement a capability as a service.
Module
One repository under openabstractions-flat/abstraction-*, stacked so a higher module builds on a lower one's guarantees, such as the model module resolving a reference before the download module moves bytes.
Service
A named wire interface and behavioral version, such as abstraction.logging/sink@1, and the endpoint inside the runtime that answers its calls — one word for the interface and the thing that answers it, as gRPC uses it. Distinct from a contract, the numbered rule set that defines its promises and limits. In the module catalogue, service is the Kind a module's definition earns by declaring a service that is not direct.
Provider
An implementation behind a capability contract that the runtime mediates. Some run inside the runtime, such as the download module's transfer agent; others are registered programs the runtime launches or attaches to, such as inventoryd, which indexes what a machine already holds, or lemonaded, which serves images, transcription and speech. In the module catalogue, provider is also a Kind value: a module named <x>-over-<y> with a command, or one whose definition declares guarantees and no service.
Runtime
The installed OA program selected for the connected local account and program. It resolves capabilities, enforces rights, owns service state, and mediates providers. It is one program, openabstractions serve runtime: installed, the platform's service manager starts it as the background service; run directly, the same command starts it in the foreground. On Windows the per-user supervisor, openabstractions serve supervisor, starts it and restarts it after a failure.
Facade
The shared entry point used to resolve typed capability clients. Machine selects and trusts the local runtime; Resolve… methods return a bound client.
Contract page
A module's CONTRACT.md: the document stating a contract's obligations, admission order and refusal reasons. Its rule ids, such as INF-A1, are what tests and refusals cite.
Requirements
The guarantees and execution placement requested during resolution. The runtime returns an eligible binding or a typed refusal.
Guarantees
Contract-specific promises required before work starts, such as recovery across caller exit. Accepted work keeps the guarantees under which it was admitted.
Placement
Requested execution location during resolution: local, remote, or any where the capability supports it; the resolved endpoint has a fixed placement.
Subject
A rights subject identifies the account and program a policy decision evaluates. A job's subject identifies the account and program that owns its submitted work. A job's subject observes, lists, reads and cancels what it submitted, with no rule consulted for that; rights and identity read the same subject when deciding or verifying a peer.
Binding
The resolved client-to-service tie: in the facade, the capability, service, provider revision, transport, endpoint, placement, and guarantees a continuation call validates against. An identity binding captures peer evidence once at accept for later rechecking. A job acceptance binding supplies receiver-established caller scope and authenticated admission evidence.
Idempotency key
A stable caller-owned key created before submission; a retry with the same key reconciles the same job instead of starting a new one.
Job
The module that gives submitted work a durable identity, acceptance, reconciliation, cancellation, and inventory: abstraction-job. Other capabilities submit through it rather than each tracking accepted work of their own. An accepted job is work a service owns; its receipt records the job identifier, logical owner, idempotency key, binding, and accepted guarantees.
Peer identity
Operating-system evidence about the connected account, process, executable, package, and code identity. Each attribute carries its proof strength.
Rights
Policy decisions for an action on a resource by a verified peer. The service that owns the resource enforces the decision.
Budget
A credential's daily spend cap, checked before a hosted call starts. A request over an exhausted budget refuses budget_exceeded.
Ceiling
The strongest proof identity can bind for an attribute.
Application manifest
An operator-installed record naming an application, its executable, display title, start guidance and optional activation recipe. A running instance announces its interfaces separately.
Application instance
A leased OA handle returned when a ready application announces itself. Renewals keep that exact instance present until withdrawal or expiry.
Application context
An application-owned document or workflow name, title, and revision. Interaction adapters use the revision to reject a call aimed at an older target.
MCP gateway
An authorized integration program that exposes a curated set of OA-backed tools to a Model Context Protocol client. Its operating-system identity determines its OA rights.
Work
What a person or application wants OA to do, before it is submitted: the plain word for the thing a job accepts and records.
Store
Where a provider keeps content. OA storage offers content-addressed objects and a combined inventory of available stores. Its local-stores provider can discover model files managed by other applications. Writes to OA-managed content use content-writer@1.
State file
The CAS state file: the lock-guarded shared state abstraction-cas maintains.
Share
A shared folder on a NAS.
Handle
An open read handle in storage, such as a POSIX file handle or a Windows HANDLE.
Sink
A destination for structured log records, exposed through abstraction.logging/sink@1. Default handlers resolve an OA logging service and report resolution failures. After a service outage, they retry with a bounded queue and report dropped records. Local fallback requires explicit provider selection.
Destination
Where a download writes bytes: a plain path outside the content store, named by the caller for a deprecated in-process download (download.Open()/Get()) and by the runtime for a job-service download, to its own result document. It never names the store.
Family
The canonical identity two names for the same weights must agree on before one of them can answer for the other, resolved by the model module. The router reads a family as the cluster of a model server's own aliases resolved to that identity, together with which servers and stores hold each one.

Yield
Giving a resource back on the service's request: a lease holder yields through Answer. What the instrument shows afterwards is the answer. An engine's own eviction is not a yield.
Resident
Loaded and currently answering calls, said of a model a model server or a model host provider is holding in memory under a lease.
Model server
A declared model runtime or provider endpoint this machine or an operator names — Ollama, LM Studio, Lemonade, or a hosted server such as OpenRouter. Registered through inference server add (inference host add until the next release) and addressed by a rights rule as host:<name> (renamed to server:<name> on the wire in a later release). abstraction-provider-modelhost's own process, which loads a model file into an engine and keeps it resident, is declared to the runtime the same way, as host:modelhost.
Host
The address part of a URL: the machine a transport connects to, as in OLLAMA_HOST or a --host flag. Distinct from a model server.
Claimed
An unverified, self-reported assertion, with no verification behind it: a peer attribute the peer itself asserted (identity's lowest proof level), a log hop the writer itself asserted (its lowest attestation standing), or a resource-table row an engine or its adapter self-reported (with no instrument behind the amount).
Location
One location in config's precedence ladder — machine, user, or process — ordered nearest first; the nearer location's value wins, and every answer carries the location it came from.
Resource
A named target for rights and for the resource module alike: credential:<name> or account as a rights target; card:<n> for an accelerator's memory (cuda:0 on CUDA, a DirectML adapter, or DRM card0), memory for system memory, or awake, the pool a wake lease claims, as one of the machine's scarce pools.
Holder
The program holding a lease or a resource amount.
Hold
One row of the resource table: an account, a program, a resource, and an amount, whether measured or claimed. A holder in two processes is two holds.
Credential manager
The abstraction.credentials/manager@1 service that registers, rotates, revokes, lists, and audits named secrets.
Operator
A person acting at the command line or the Panel, distinct from an application. Also the generated *Operator services (abstraction.rights/operator@1, abstraction.asks/operator@1, and others) that such a person, or a program the installation trusts as one, reaches through an explicitly authorized typed-peer callback.
Deprecated
A still-shipped earlier interface, each kept with its removal release named, or without one until then. The embedded file-reading config provider (Go config.go, Python python/abstraction_config.py) is kept for a deliberate out-of-tree adopter that reads configuration files directly instead of the service; Load, Watch, and JobStore are its deprecated names. Job's file-backed record interface (Store, shipped as NewFileStore) is deprecated the same way.
Inference gateway
A loopback OpenAI- and Anthropic-shaped listener on the runtime, for a program that only knows a base URL and an API key. It stays off by default; an issued gateway key binds one program.
Gateway key
The key the inference gateway issues to one program so it can reach the runtime through the gateway. A hosted server's own credential is instead called an API key.
Alias
A model's name as a model server reports it. Used as a family's identity when no store descriptor names one (family_source: alias); an alias reaches a store's own name for the same content by one matching function.
Servable
Able to serve a request for a model, unlike a store that only holds it. A component such as a projector or a VAE is never servable on its own.
Up
Whether a hosted server's listing could be read. False, with a why reason, when its credential could not be applied or its wire kind is unsupported.
Hosted
A model server reached off this machine rather than resolved locally. Pick's hosted outcome names one answering instead of a local server; its entry names a base URL, a wire kind, and a credential name.
Held in
The storage inventory stores holding an object a family or alias matches, in store order; empty when no configured store reports the model.
Domain
The remote runtime name a listed server answers through, distinguishing a remote runtime's own servers from this machine's.
Instrument
The platform mechanism that measures a resource's holders, such as Windows' GPU process memory counters. A row above its declared threshold is measured; below it, or with no instrument for a resource, the row is claimed.
Engine
The program that loads model weights and answers calls, such as llama-server, sd-server or Lemonade. A provider module wraps an engine the machine has, or OA supplies one as its own registered provider process. The model host and the Lemonade provider run publishers' pinned builds staged from archives a person or Setup downloads, and the model host's PyTorch engine, which OA wrote, is moving into its own provider module.
Lend
Writing a link into another application's engine directory so that engine serves an object already in a store, gated by abstraction.storage/lend@1. Never a move, a rename, or a deletion.
Ledger
The record of which lends are in force, oldest first; replaced in one rename, so a reader sees a whole ledger or the one before it. It says whether a lend is in force, not the engine's own list.
Object
A store's content, named the way the storage inventory names it: a store and an id, never a path.
Locator
An object's location a store reports when it published no manifest id; the ledger records the manifest id where the source published one, and the locator otherwise.
Inventory
The composed, read-only list of what objects a machine's stores hold, served by abstraction.storage/inventory@1 from designated abstraction.storage/inventory-source@1 providers, such as local-stores' own indexer.
Storage class
A retention promise: data, cache, tmp, or logs.
Retention
How long a class keeps an object once nothing holds it.
Max use
The most bytes a class may occupy.
Collector
The runtime's process that removes what a class no longer promises to keep.
Low free space
The collector's pressure trigger: 15% of the file system, capped at 4G.
Purgeable
A cache object marked for the platform cleaner.
No-backup
A folder's or object's attribute excluding it from backup.
Adopter
An application that calls OA's abstractions, such as OpenCode or ComfyUI through their OA integrations. OA publishes labelled, versioned builds of some adopters.
Question
A service-held request with offered answers. Legacy application@1 uses a fixed catalogue; ordinary application@2 carries app-authored choices with explicit replay bounds. Ordinary answers select app behavior; first-use permission answers have exact Rights effects.
Rule
A stored authorization entry: a subject, an action, a resource, and permit or deny. Contracts say rule; the Panel and this site say permission.
Permission
A rule as the Panel shows it, with Allow and Block for permit and deny.
Responder
A program a person lets answer first-use questions on their behalf through abstraction.asks/responder@1, under an exact rule that expires. It never answers a question about itself.
Modality
What a model server serves: chat, embed, transcription, speech, image, video or live. The wire still says profile, as in profile:image, until its next service version.
Content scope
The content an application may write and read for one kind of input or output, such as output:image for generated pictures or input:audio for audio to transcribe. One first-use allow writes both rights on it.
Provider kit
The shared Go packages under abstraction-inference/go/providerhost that provider programs build on: engine-file proofs, clean launch environments, loopback checks, and request checks for engines such as sd-server.
Awake
The wake level that keeps the system on, held as a wake lease on the resource awake. Today the lease takes a platform request only while its holder also holds a card lease, and that request keeps the display on as well. In 0.4.0 a provider that declares a card holds it for the work it serves, a provisional exception that a lease held for the requesting application replaces after research.
Awake (display)
awake:display, the wake level that keeps the display on and holds off the screen saver and automatic lock. Decided as its own rule per application and not built yet.
Selection policy
A saved, ordered list of eligible models and model servers for one account and program. A chat@2 or image@2 request names one in place of a model, and the runtime picks an available candidate from it.
Preset
The generation settings a provider keeps for a model, such as steps, guidance, scheduler and size. A caller who wants another preset names another model.

Service lifecycle

From a requirement to a bound call

  1. Connect. A language facade selects the installed runtime for the current account and establishes the shared native IPC transport.
  2. Resolve. The client sends a capability, accepted services, guarantees, and placement to Resolver.Resolve.
  3. Authorize and select. The runtime identifies the caller, checks policy, and selects an eligible ready candidate.
  4. Bind. A generated client receives a service reference with one contract, endpoint, placement, and provider binding.
  5. Call. The generated client validates records and uses the shared transport. The OA service owns downstream provider connections and credentials.
  6. Continue. Accepted jobs remain associated with their original owner and binding. Observation, cancellation, and reconciliation use that association.

Go resolution shape

machine := facade.Discover()
logs, err := machine.ResolveLog(ctx, facade.Requirements{
    Scope: facade.ScopeLocal,
})
if err != nil { /* inspect the typed binding error */ }
logs.Write(record)

Left unset, Requirements.Scope resolves as any; set local or remote explicitly to restrict placement.

A later resolution may choose another eligible provider. An existing binding stays specific to the selected service. The facade contract defines resolution, trust, and binding behavior.

Authority

Identity, rights, and execution are separate facts

QuestionSource of the answerWhere it matters
Who connected?Native transport evidence captured by Identity, with proof attached to every attribute.Runtime selection, caller isolation, policy lookup, and audit.
May this caller act?Authorization.Decide or DecideFor under abstraction.rights/authorization@1.The service that owns the resource enforces the result before access or mutation.
Who executes the work?The service deployment and its configured provider.File access, network access, process lifetime, and provider credentials.
Is this the intended service?Runtime endpoint selection plus the transport's server-trust policy.Before sending requests or secrets.

Caller-supplied labels remain metadata. Provider names, model names, MCP client names, application titles, and context titles carry no identity authority. Credential values stay in the credential service and are applied to an exact target through Applier.Check and Applier.Apply.

Durable work

Acceptance, observation, and recovery

Prepare identity first

Create the idempotency key before sending work. Equal duplicate submissions recover the original receipt.

GetHistoryWindow · Submit · Reconcile

Separate waiting from work

Canceling a transport wait ends that wait. Explicit work cancellation uses CancelWork with the original idempotency key.

ObserveWork · CancelWork

Treat a lost reply as uncertain

Reconnect to the original logical owner and call Reconcile. A new idempotency key would describe new work.

AcceptanceResult · Receipt

Respect continuity signals

Opaque cursors belong to one provider instance and caller subject. A gap asks the caller to restart from a current snapshot or recover through a contract-specific path.

cursor · epoch · gap

The job contract defines accepted-work ownership, reconciliation, explicit cancellation, retained results, and inventory bounds.

Applications and assistants

Application MCP: shared document state, declared actions and native mediation explains the developing 0.8.0 profile and its availability.

Directory metadata, activation, and tools have distinct roles

Register / RemoveAn authorized operator manages persistent manifests and activation recipes.
Announce / WithdrawA ready application creates and renews a leased instance with interface and context metadata.
ObserveA caller lists only manifests and live instances visible under its rights.
ActivateThe runtime starts a registered executable and waits for a fresh announcement from the eligible local session. Canceling the wait leaves the user application running.

These methods belong to abstraction.facade/applications@2. An interface entry describes an application-owned protocol such as comfy.presentation@1. Metadata does not invoke that protocol.

An application interaction adapter implements the protocol and preserves the selected instance, context, and revision through preview, apply, and readback. A stale revision refuses an outdated target. This adapter is specific to the application interface.

An MCP gateway maps a curated tool set onto OA clients and application adapters. The MCP gateway runs as its own verified integration subject and receives explicit rights. It exposes a selected tool set rather than generic forwarding to arbitrary MCP servers or application methods.

Failure and recovery

Read the typed result before retrying

ResultMeaningCaller response
forbiddenThe resolution boundary's own peer check: a different account, or a caller that cannot be verified.Run the program as the runtime's own account. No capability-specific rule is read yet.
not_permittedA verified caller's own rights rule refuses the action or resource, decided inside the call.Change the grant or choose an allowed action; see inference's Set up a model server for a worked grant.
not_ready / unavailableThe required service or provider cannot serve the call now.Observe readiness or retry within the contract's bounds.
unmet_requirementsNo eligible candidate supplies every requested guarantee or placement.Install or configure a suitable provider, or revise the requirement explicitly.
unsupportedThe selected contract lacks the requested optional behavior.Use a supported method or resolve a contract that declares it.
invalidInput violates the contract's shape, bound, state, or identifier rules.Correct the request. Repeating the same bytes gives the same refusal.
stale / conflictA revision or compare-and-set base no longer names the current state.Read the current state and decide again.
gapRetained history cannot prove continuous delivery from the supplied cursor.Restart from a current snapshot or use the contract's recovery method.
uncertain / unknownThe caller lacks evidence of the effect or accepted work.Reconcile with the same idempotency key or read current state before acting.

Each contract owns its exact enum and recovery rule. The table is a navigation aid across recurring meanings.

Asks

Retain bounded requests and answers. Applications own ordinary choice UI; OA owns permission presentation.

abstraction.asks/application@1 abstraction.asks/application@2 abstraction.asks/operator@1

Caller-scoped Answer/Dismiss is integrated at ed97c10f8; the Go terminal example is integrated at f27944846. Ordinary agent delegation remains planned. Acknowledgement confirms an already-recorded answer. Asking requires explicit abstraction.asks/question.ask on account.

Inference

Bind model chat, embeddings, transcription, speech, live audio, image generation, and operator controls to mediated providers. Video generation runs as durable inference work through Jobs.

abstraction.inference/chat@1 abstraction.inference/embed@1 abstraction.inference/transcription@1 abstraction.inference/speech@1 abstraction.inference/live@1 abstraction.inference/image@1 abstraction.inference/operator@1

Facade: ResolveInference, ResolveEmbeddings, ResolveInferenceOperator. Generated clients bind the other modality endpoints.

Complete is Stream's non-streaming twin, observing a call to its end and folding the deltas into one reply. Complete names the Go method below; abstraction.inference/complete names the rights action the runtime checks inside it.

chat, err := facade.Discover().ResolveInference(ctx, facade.Requirements{})
// forbidden here is the resolution boundary's own peer check, not a missing grant
reply, err := chat.Complete(ctx, wire.Request{Model: "llama3.1", Messages: msgs})
fmt.Println(reply.Outcome) // not_permitted is a missing per-server grant, CONTRACT.md INF-A2

The same service through the inference gateway, for a program that only speaks the OpenAI or Anthropic API:

openabstractions inference gateway on --address 127.0.0.1:8765
openabstractions inference key issue --for /absolute/path/to/curl
curl http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer oalk_..." \
  -d '{"model":"llama3.1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in five words."}]}'
