Requests and presentation

App choices, OA permissions and notification actions

Applications show ordinary choices in their own UI. OA keeps shared pending and answer state and presents its permission requests. Notifications with actions form a separate planned native surface.

The permission journey connects two identified apps, native consent, a saved rule and an actual credential-bearing operation. Identity binds the calling program, Rights decides access, Asks retains the proposed decision and answer, and the resource service checks and performs the operation. The canonical guide preserves the research basis, accepted one/all scope and finite full-control design; the runnable Windows/macOS playground and human captures remain pending.

Development source for 0.4.0, October 5, 2026. Released 0.3.0 has its own contents and package evidence. Automatic OA ordinary popups are removed; caller-scoped Answer/Dismiss and the Go terminal example are integrated. Fresh native Mac verification and ordinary agent answering remain open.

InteractionExampleOwner and state
App-owned ordinary choiceReplace an output, or choose a model for one requestThe application's normal window, CLI or controls. The Go terminal example uses OA's pending/observation/own-answer/replay API. ComfyUI keeps model selection in its existing node controls.
OA-owned permissionAllow one program to submit downloads or read a shared resourceOA's native dialog explains requester, recorded publisher, scope, effect and duration. The Windows 11 renderer is integrated, with bounded native guards passed. Final visual acceptance and system/privacy forms remain open.
Notification with actionsA completed job offers Open to its Activity recordA compact native notification with attribution and an expiring service-owned action. Public posting/action lifecycle and the complete application journey remain planned.

Native appearance follows the actual OS version: Windows 10, Windows 11 or AppKit on macOS. The Windows 11 renderer has bounded expanded details and compact chrome. Successful permission answers finish without a second confirmation dialog; failed or uncertain completion retains its report.

Synthetic native lifetime/answer guards and result-report checks passed for the compact Windows 11 source through 957df22bd, using a fake Rights owner. The owner's screenshot shows earlier baseline 3c3b31abf; final appearance of the compact revision remains unaccepted. Keyboard/UIA, cross-monitor DPI/high contrast, Windows 10 appearance, actual owner Mac answering/effect/Undo, lock/unlock, installed login/upgrade and 0.4.0 release qualification remain open.

Planned system access permissions explain a protected system act and use the operating system's administrator approval when required. Planned privacy access permissions explain the device or data capability and follow its platform-specific consent and Settings path. Windows owns actual UAC approval and its secure desktop.

A stable action code and structured resource identify authority. Readable descriptions and display groups explain it. Routine, sensitive and administrative tiers decide who may answer under the existing first-use policy; an administrative OA tier alone supplies no OS elevation requirement. Publisher verification describes recorded identity evidence, with an unverified publisher indicating an evidence gap.

The accepted common permission schema defines explicit operations and typed targets. Source e5c1eebb1 integrates 34 compiled built-in action definitions, the Credentials-owned typed named Use resource and shared native/web first-use explanations. Named Use follows the current account-owned name slot through rotation or recreated registration, under its current host/consumer restrictions.

An isolated native IPC/loopback test passed missing permission → exact caller-bound ask → recorded Allow/applied permit → retry using the named secret. The fixture answered through the operator API; human native interaction retains its separate limits above. Typed one/all selectors, versioned full control, breadth-warning presentation, raw secret Read and the protected OS helper remain unimplemented. Breadth warnings describe scope separately from actual OS elevation.

The Go terminal example prints the full destination, submits its own selection and observes the retained service winner before its guarded output effect. Its suite and Windows redirected-input runtime checks passed; actual console typing remains manual acceptance, and Linux/macOS checks are compile-only.

Ordinary answers select app behavior and grant no OA permission. The proven requester can Answer/Dismiss only its own immutable RequestRef; account-wide answering requires an explicitly authorized operator. Program attribution establishes no human presence. Acknowledge confirms an exact existing answer and relinquishes full service replay. Routine first-use responder enrollment supplies no ordinary answering authority. See ASK-A9, ASK-W5 and ASK-O9 for the current service boundaries.

On-demand desktop Panel

The Panel, section by section

The Panel installs with the runtime and opens as a native window on Windows, macOS and Linux. Each of its sections links to its own anchor below: a "Learn more" link on Windows, a small "?" mark next to the heading on macOS and Linux, and a round "?" button for the current page as a whole. Every anchor names what the section does, the contract rule that decides it, and its command-line equivalent where one exists today.

Status

Service check

Rereads the resolved runtime's capability readiness, the call status also makes. Runtime selection and trust follow the rule status and rights both use: an explicit endpoint is never trusted as the installed runtime without its own registration proof.

The runtime is the shared background service every application on this account uses through OpenAbstractions. It runs work in the background, tracks the models and credentials an application may use, and holds the questions it is waiting for you to answer. A pending question appears under Questions and permissions; a download in progress appears under Work.

openabstractions status

Services provided

Shows registered programs that provide services to applications. Manage providers opens the runtime's registered-provider view, which retains each provider's role, services and readiness.

Codex connection

Add OpenAbstractions to the account's shared Codex setup. This affects Codex desktop, CLI and IDE, rather than one project. Confirm the permission request and restart Codex after adding it. Removing the saved entry preserves OA jobs and permissions.

Claude Code connections

Apps opens the connection setup and the saved-connection list. Each saved entry belongs to its exact project, helper and name. A saved entry does not establish Claude approval, a live connection, OpenAbstractions permission or message delivery.

Setup uses the product's supported extension mechanism. A project connection chooses its folder through the native picker. Open Claude requests the registered desktop application; choose Code there and check again. Missing or ambiguous program information stays unavailable.

OpenAbstractions asks for permissions through its normal native questions. Removing a saved connection leaves jobs, permissions, vendor login and the product's independent lifetime with their owners. Unknown information clears current connection claims; a displayed historical outcome is labelled separately.

Background messages

A separate native review approves the background companion's message-header checks. Reading message text and replying retain their own permissions. Approval and configuration leave actual reception unconfirmed. Reset removes the companion and only the approval this setup added.

Background Asks

A separate native review approves observation of eligible questions and shared choices while Claude is idle. Answering requires its own enrollment, and person-only permissions stay with the person. Message approval covers messages.

Work

Model requests

Lists retained model requests using the Activity range and app filters, with additional filters for computer, model and result. Each row names the computer, model server, model and result recorded for that request. Missing computer history reads Not recorded; an unavailable read does not establish that no requests occurred.

Agent exits

Shows retained exit records for the selected Claude or Codex connection. The currently kept helper's native identity scopes the history read; record text is display content. Exit history describes past runs.

Work started from this Panel

Lists the jobs this Panel itself submitted, with each job's current state and display label. A job belongs to the program that submitted it (JOB-A1); this view shows only this Panel's own.

openabstractions jobs list

Work started by apps

Lists the jobs every application on this account submitted. Seeing them needs abstraction.job/inventory.read; canceling another app's job needs abstraction.job/acceptance.cancel (JOB-A1).

openabstractions jobs list --all, or jobs cancel --all <id> to cancel one

Notifications

Lists each app that notified you in the last seven days with its count, beside a switch. Turning an app off sets a block on abstraction.asks/notification.post for it and withdraws its shown notifications; turning it on removes that block. Below are the notifications the runtime holds now and what became of each (ASK-N6).

Messages

Shows the runtime's retained message activity and outcomes. App names and message text are untrusted display content. Technical details keep routing identifiers separate from the visible names.

Read one message

Open message asks the runtime for that message's retained text under the Panel's current authority. Closing the reader, leaving the page, hiding the window or reaching expiry clears the displayed text. A refusal or unavailable runtime does not establish that the message was deleted.

Download a file

Submits an HTTP(S) transfer to the runtime's job service by URL, digest and size, and recovers a saved request after a lost reply instead of resubmitting it. A dropped connection keeps its error, and the next attempt resumes from the last proven byte (DL-E1).

openabstractions download <url> --sha256 HEX --size BYTES

Questions and permissions

Questions

Shows pending and past legacy permission requests and ordinary app requests through separate public records. Authorized operators can answer or dismiss them. Ordinary dismissal records a terminal decision without selecting an option or changing permissions. App-owned presentation and its caller-scoped answer route follow the current service boundary.

The hidden session presenter supplies OA permission prompts without a persistent tray or menu-bar icon; the Panel opens on demand. The permission journey explains the native request and its retained effect.

Answering access

Choose a native app to answer routine questions from your apps. Review the listed classes it may answer and the sensitive and administrative questions that always come to you, then confirm. Answering access ends after 30 days without an answer. Shared script hosts are ineligible.

Answered for you shows the app and answer, with Undo for permissions it granted. Revoke answering access stops new answers; existing permissions keep their expiry. Select Also revoke permissions granted through this app to remove those permissions too.

Permissions

Allows or blocks one action for one account and application on one resource, at the policy revision shown. Every decision the runtime makes is checked again at call time under abstraction.rights/authorization@1; a Panel edit leaves a decision already made as it was.

The open view refreshes after another operator changes policy. Unsaved drafts retain their original revision for explicit review. Expiry is checked through current rule reads; time alone does not change the durable policy revision. Applications are checked against these rules every time they act.

The permission journey distinguishes Block, removing one rule and effective access, with broader selectors and fixed full control identified as pending design.

openabstractions rights list, or rights grant

Messages between agents

With Ask me first on, the first message from one of your agents to another raises a permission question, and your Allow or Don't allow is saved for that direction. With Ask me first off, Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode that you keep message each other without that question. An answer you saved for one direction still applies either way. Ask me first is on after a fresh install, and only the Panel can turn it.

A message from another agent never answers a question for you. Permission questions, including the ones an agent raises, are answered by you.

Device

Holders

Shows who is using a limited resource on this device right now: the app, the account, how much, and whether it was measured or claimed. Verified rows are measured. A claimed row's amount is 0 unless the row is a lease, and then it is the grant the runtime wrote (RES-T3). A resource named card:<n> can report the same bytes as system memory on shared-memory hardware. A reader never sums two resources, or a verified row with a claimed one (RES-T5). Each graphics driver reset of the last seven days that a provider declaring a graphics card reported is one row naming the engines it stopped and whether the running request is paused (RES-G6).

openabstractions resources

Keeping this device awake

Lists each app that keeps this device awake now or has a rule about it. A holder that also leases a graphics card keeps the display on too (RES-A1). The switch allows the app or stops it. Stopping writes a deny on abstraction.resource/hold for awake, and a stopped app's wake leases end. Allowing writes a permit. Permissions… opens the app's rules, where Remove rule returns it to the default.

openabstractions resources awake

Storage

One row per storage class with how long it is kept: temporary files end with the work that used them (STO-T7), cache is removed only after you confirm (STO-T4), logs keep up to 10% of the drive, at most 4 GB, oldest first (LOG-S14), and data stays until you remove it (STO-T1). Sizes per class and Clean now wait on a storage operation that reports them.

Inference

Model servers and spend

Lists the model servers this device calls directly for model completions, separate from the gateway keys other apps use to reach it, with whether each is reachable and its spend today against its daily budget; adds or removes a model server. A hosted server's credential is applied to each outgoing request and never cached (INF-C1).

openabstractions inference server list, or inference server add / inference server remove

Inference gateway

Turns on the inference gateway, a local proxy other apps on this account can call, so an app that already speaks the OpenAI or Anthropic API reaches this device with no code changes. It listens only on 127.0.0.1, stays off by default, and stays set after a restart. Changing it needs the rule inference server manage (abstraction.inference/host.manage).

openabstractions inference gateway on --address 127.0.0.1:PORT, or inference gateway off

Gateway keys

Issues or revokes a gateway key, which lets one other app reach this device through the inference gateway; the key is shown once and this Panel never stores it. A key alone grants nothing: the app still needs inference complete (abstraction.inference/complete) on a model server and permission to apply a hosted server's credential.

openabstractions inference key issue --for PATH, or inference key revoke

Providers

Model servers

Lists every model server the runtime can reach and which app or file registered each one: something you configured, an app's own record, a built-in default, or another trusted runtime.

openabstractions inference server list

Registered providers

Lists every registered provider and its role (a managed process, a model server, or a remote runtime) with its activation, services, endpoint and readiness. Every registration is providers/<name>.json in the runtime's own state (FAC-R1).

openabstractions provider list, or provider add / provider remove

Model selection policies

Reads, saves or deletes one named, ordered model preference for this Panel or a selected application. Other-application edits require the separate account-wide selection.manage_for permission. An optional provider value pins a candidate to a logical provider declaration; the runtime still checks caller identity, permission, provider readiness and model availability when the application makes a call.

No command-line equivalent yet.

Remote runtimes

Lists model servers reported by another trusted runtime in its own domain; their credentials stay on that runtime and are never copied here. Trusting a remote runtime's report follows the same registration rule as a local one (FAC-R1).

No command-line equivalent yet.

Credentials

Connect a service

Saves a hosted service's key, such as DeepSeek or OpenRouter, and adds its model server with a daily budget chosen from a list: money for a service whose replies carry their cost, such as OpenRouter, and tokens for one whose replies carry only token counts, such as DeepSeek. Each row shows today's spend and the budget, which the service enforces before any request is sent (INF-C2). An app then uses the gateway address shown here as its base URL with any key; the key stays in OpenAbstractions (INF-W4, INF-W5). An app's first use asks you, and the gateway holds its call until you answer (INF-W10).

openabstractions inference server add <name> --base URL --api openai-compatible --credential <name>

Saved credentials

Lists every credential registered on this account: its name, kind, status, targets, consumers and where it's used. The secret itself is typed in once and never shown, logged or sent back.

openabstractions credentials list

Add credential

Registers a name that isn't already in use, scoped to the hosts it may be sent to and the apps allowed to apply it. The credential manager binds the caller the same way for every write (CRED-H1).

openabstractions credentials add <name> --target HOST --for CONSUMER

Rotate

Replaces the secret and expiry for a name you've already listed, at the revision the list showed.

openabstractions credentials rotate <name>

Revoke

Deletes the secret right away and keeps a record that it existed, at the revision you've already listed.

openabstractions credentials revoke <name>

App access

Sets whether one app on one account can use a credential, through the rule credentials apply (abstraction.credentials/apply) on that credential; it's the same rule editor as Questions and permissions. Listing and editing it needs this Panel to hold credentials manage (abstraction.credentials/holder.manage) and credentials list (abstraction.credentials/holder.read) (CRED-A2).

openabstractions credentials allow <name> --program PATH, or add --deny

Settings, logging, identity and explore

Settings

Reads and writes your settings and watches them for later changes. Each value says where it came from: for you, for this device, or for this run. A value's source follows the location order process over user over machine (CFG-R1); an environment variable overrides for that process only, and an empty one is no override (CFG-W3).

Disabled download delegates switches the nas and bits delegates off on this device. The two job directory rows are deprecated. Watching settings for changes does not touch what you are editing. If settings change while you are editing, save your draft first, then read again. Pause, resume, download destinations and host refusal files are set from the openabstractions command line for now.

No command-line equivalent yet.

Logging

Reads the runtime's retained log history, filtered by program and level, and can follow new records as they arrive. Each record's hop 0 is the process that wrote it; later hops are what each next service could verify about that write (LOG-I1).

A claim an application makes about itself is unverified. A stamp this runtime's logging service adds itself is verified.

No command-line equivalent yet.

Identity

Shows which runtime this device selected, how it bound this Panel's own connection, and what this platform can prove about a caller. A bound attribute is proven by native transport evidence, or left unbound where the platform cannot prove it (ID-B1).

No command-line equivalent yet.

Explore

Calls a capability as this Panel and shows the result beside the rights rule that allowed or blocked it, so a grant or a revoke can be tried again without leaving the page. This is the same call probe makes, including a probe marked writes, which asks before it runs.

Grant or revoke the deciding rule for an application directly from a result, then try the call again. This Panel can only act as itself here; to test another application, run a copy of openabstractions named openabstractions-probe under that application's own path.

openabstractions probe <capability> [action]

Compare the APIs

The same event in your language

These examples write a structured log event through an already resolved client. Select a language to compare its native API. The calling application handles any returned error or exception.

import (
    "context"
    "log/slog"
    logging "github.com/openabstractions/abstraction-logging/go/client"
)

func recordStart(ctx context.Context, events *logging.Client) error {
    return events.LogContext(ctx, int64(slog.LevelInfo), "worker started",
        map[string]string{"component": "worker"})
}
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from abstraction.logging import Record, Sink

def record_start(events: Sink) -> None:
    events.write(Record(
        schema=1,
        time=datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"),
        level=0,
        msg="worker started",
        attrs={"component": "worker"},
    ))
#include <abstraction/logging/client.hpp>

void record_start(const abstraction::logging::Logger& events) {
    events.log(0, "worker started", {{"component", "worker"}});
}

Supply the current UTC timestamp in RFC 3339 format.

use abstraction_logging_api::{Record, Sink};

fn record_start<S: Sink>(events: &S, timestamp: String) -> Result<(), S::Error> {
    events.write(Record {
        schema: 1,
        time: timestamp,
        level: 0,
        msg: "worker started".into(),
        attrs: [("component".into(), "worker".into())].into(),
        ..Default::default()
    })
}
import {newRecord} from '@openabstractions/logging';

/** @param {import('@openabstractions/logging').SinkClient} events */
async function recordStart(events) {
    const record = newRecord();
    record.schema = 1n;
    record.time = new Date().toISOString();
    record.level = 0n;
    record.msg = "worker started";
    record.attrs = {component: "worker"};
    await events.write(record);
}

One-way logging confirms local submission. A storage receipt is not returned. For connection setup, use the language guides. For other operations, open the capability’s generated schema in the API index.
